About this item

  • PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) - Get super sharp image clarity on your 4K TV using AI enhanced resolution for ultra-high definition play with astonishing detail
  • Optimized Console Performance - Reach higher and more consistent frame rates for silky smooth gameplay with support for 60Hz and 120Hz displays.
  • Advanced Ray Tracing - Experience next level realism with ray traced reflections, shadows, and high-quality global illumination as you explore stunning game worlds
  • 2TB of Storage - Keep your favorite games ready and waiting for you to jump in and play with 2TB of SSD storage built in
  • PS5 Pro Game Boost and Backwards Compatibility - The PS5 Pro console can play over 8,500 PS4 games. With the PS5 Pro version of the Game Boost feature, you can even enjoy faster and smoother frame rates in some of the PS4 and PS5 console’s greatest games

How customer reviews and ratings work

Customer Reviews, including Product Star Ratings, help customers to learn more about the product and decide whether it is the right product for them.

To calculate the overall star rating and percentage breakdown by star, we don’t use a simple average. Instead, our system considers things like how recent a review is and if the reviewer bought the item on Amazon. It also analyses reviews to verify trustworthiness.

Amazon Customer
5 out of 5 stars
Excellent on my 8K Samsung TV
The PlayStation 5 Pro is an impressive upgrade for gamers looking to push visual quality and immersion to new heights. Designed for upto 8K TVs, the PS5 Pro's hardware enhancements allow for a higher graphical fidelity with options for 8K at 60Hz and 4K at 120Hz, delivering stunning visuals that truly stand out on compatible displays. A standout feature is its improved ray tracing capabilities, which enable realistic lighting and reflections across several games. This enhancement brings added depth and realism to scenes, especially in games like Spider-Man 2 and Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered, where the visuals now appear sharper and smoother. The new PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) technology also supports upscaling, giving even 4K displays an extra visual boost by delivering crisper textures without overburdening the GPU​​​​. In addition to visuals, the PS5 Pro performs impressively in terms of heat management and Wi-Fi 7 support. It runs quieter and cooler than previous models, even after extended gaming sessions, which is a notable upgrade over the original PS5. The added Wi-Fi 7 capability boosts download speeds significantly for those with compatible routers, providing faster connectivity and smoother online gameplay​​​​. Overall, the PS5 Pro offers substantial improvements for visual immersion and performance, making it a great choice for tech enthusiasts looking to maximize their gaming setup, especially on 8K TVs. However, its high price may be a factor for some, given that the original PS5 already delivers impressive quality.

  • Randi Rabbit
    5 out of 5 stars
    PS5 Pro – Worth Every Penny!
    Reviewed in the United Kingdom on 30 January 2025
    Edition: Console
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    I’ll be honest, I was on the fence about spending £700 on the PS5 Pro, but now that I’ve made the upgrade, I can confidently say it was absolutely worth it. All of my reservations have been completely alleviated, and I’m blown away by the improvements over the standard PS5.

    First and foremost, the performance is phenomenal. The increased processing power means faster load times, smoother gameplay, and a noticeable boost in graphics quality. Games that looked great before now look absolutely stunning on the PS5 Pro. I’m talking about richer details, sharper textures, and better lighting effects that really immerse you in the experience.

    The upscaled 4K visuals are a game-changer, and I’ve noticed a major improvement in frame rates. Whether I’m playing fast-paced action games or open-world adventures, the PS5 Pro handles everything flawlessly. The new ray tracing enhancements add another level of realism that I didn’t even realize I was missing before.

    The upgraded cooling system is another standout feature. The console runs quieter and stays cooler, even when I’m gaming for extended hours. No more worrying about the system getting too hot or loud during intense gaming sessions.

    The design is sleek and modern, and the console feels incredibly sturdy. It fits seamlessly into my entertainment setup, and I love the subtle but noticeable differences in build quality that the Pro offers over the standard model.

    One of the biggest surprises for me was how future-proof the PS5 Pro feels. With the increased hardware capabilities, I know I’m set for the next few years of gaming without worrying about performance issues. It’s a solid investment that will keep delivering top-tier gaming experiences as new titles release.

    All in all, I’m incredibly satisfied with my purchase. The PS5 Pro has exceeded my expectations in every way, and I’m thrilled I decided to make the upgrade. If you’re on the fence, I’d say go for it—you won’t regret it.

  • Sot
    5 out of 5 stars
    PS5 Pro Review – “A Real Upgrade, Not Just a Flex”
    Reviewed in the United Kingdom on 3 December 2025
    Edition: Console
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    The PS5 Pro isn’t just a shinier version of the original — it’s genuinely the better choice if you care about performance. The upgraded GPU makes a noticeable difference in games that support 4K/120 or higher dynamic resolutions. Visual clarity is sharper, motion is cleaner, and demanding titles finally feel like they’re running the way they were meant to.

    What surprised me most is the improved frame pacing. Even when a game isn’t hitting its highest target, it’s more consistent, which makes a bigger difference than people think. HDR performance is also better — brighter highlights, cleaner contrast, and fewer muddy dark scenes.

    The Pro’s new “Performance Mode” in supported games gives you actual options now, not just a slightly louder fan. Speaking of noise: it runs cooler and quieter under heavy load than my standard PS5 ever did.

    If you play competitive shooters, action games, or anything fast-paced, the upgrade is absolutely worth it. If you just use your PS5 casually, the standard still holds up — but for anyone who wants the best possible performance without jumping to a PC, the PS5 Pro is the clear pick. It delivers meaningful improvements, not marketing fluff.

    5 out of 5 stars
    Great upgrade for gaming / tech enthusiasts
    Reviewed in the United Kingdom on 11 November 2025
    Edition: Console
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    As a long time gamer (console, handeld and PC) who has tried to keep up with the latest and greatest over the years I was in a position where I was finally able to upgrade my PS5 to the PS5 Pro

    My personal preference in gaming is the best framerates, I don't care much for 4k. I would much prefer 60fps at 1080p over 30fps at 4k. However the console gaming market seems to prioritise 4k 30fps and performance modes in a lot of games struggle to hit 60fps on my regular PS5

    I went into this purchase with optimism hoping to see the reward of the costs, and I am pleased to say that I am impressed with the results.

    I've played Final Fantasy 7 rebirth on both consoles and on PS5 Pro it looks like a completely different game I can play at 60fps and the game looks as you would expect (on ps5 the resolution would be so low that objects and characters would be blurry)

    Other major games I've played in the short time since purchase are Borderlands 4 and Ghost of Yotei.

    Borderlands has looked amazing the whole time crisp 60fps even during hectic combat in the massive open world.

    Ghost of Yotei is a real testament to what the ps5 pro can do, the performance pro setting exclusive to ps5 pro is a buttery smooth 60fps with ray tracing lighting enable for an ultra realistic experience as you explore the world and it sets a high bar for other ps5 pro games to come

    The 2TB storage is a welcome addition too I can have more games installed without worry of having to make space

    Overall the upgrade for a dedicated gamer is worth it, it could have been nice to include the 4k disc drive but I did purchase it as I still have physical media

    If you are a casual gamer or not too fussed about getting the absolute best performance and happy with "good enough" then the standard ps5 is probably better for you

    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    I saw a lot of bad reviews of people saying that they don't notice the difference between this Pro version and the PS5. Well I do. There's a huge difference but you have to be like me, an enthusiastic or freak person who loves to play the games in 4K and with a high frame rate. And play close to the TV too to enjoy the details. First I tested some PS4 games and I feel an improvement. They looked sharper, even more colourful and also with a smoother gameplay. So definitely it is an improvement there. For this you need to activate the PS4 games enhancer option and the VRR for games that don't have VRR. So first things first. You need a proper 4K TV 120hz with VRR and game mode with HDR on to notice all these improvements. In that game mode you can se the FPS. Yesterday I was playing The Last of Us Part I in the Pro Mode at 80/90 FPS. It just looks so beautiful and smooth. It is an absolute pleasure to play this way. It is like play the fidelity mode on PS5 (which was locked at 30fps) at 80/90fps! Just awesome. Then I played other games that has not the pro enhanced label and they look and perform much better. You can play Dirt 5 on the fidelity mode at 60fps, also Cyberpunk looks and performs much better, God of War at 90fps with better graphics too... It improves every game. It's an absolute joy to play games this way. But yeah, as someone mentioned in the reviews, you need a nice TV for this (4K, 120hz, VRR and Game mode with HDR). And you need to be a freak that appreciates the best things in life and the little details. Otherwise, don't waste your money. PS5 still a superb console.
